summary: Pooles Island Light, Harford County, Maryland: a granite tower of 1825, decommissioned in 1939, inside Aberdeen Proving Ground, solar-relit in 2011.

light.note: Solar-powered flashing light from 2011 (directory, LighthouseFriends); pattern from the directory

lens.note: Fourth-order lens: 1855 per LighthouseFriends and the archive; the National Register form dates a fourth-order Fresnel lamp to 1899. Lens removed at decommissioning in 1939.

structures.note: National Register form: total height 40 ft 6 in; the archive gives 30 ft from base to lantern
34 by 20 ft stone house, second story 1883; all above-ground remnants removed

staffing.note: National Register form: automated 1917. LighthouseFriends: last keeper removed in 1918.

access.note: Inside Aberdeen Proving Ground. Closed. Live ordnance reported. Reached only by boat. Do not land.

events.note: Act of 26 May 1824 authorized lighthouses on Thomas Point and Pooles Island
Granite conical tower and stone keeper's house; contract signed 16 April 1825 with John Donohoo and Simon Frieze
Fog bell and tower placed on the property; Congress earmarked $2,800 (LighthouseFriends)
Inspector found the fog bell too weak to be heard more than a mile (LighthouseFriends)
Fourth-order Fresnel lens (LighthouseFriends, archive); NRHP dates a fourth-order Fresnel lamp to 1899
Lamps upgraded with new and improved lanterns
Fog-bell tower rebuilt (NRHP); LighthouseFriends dates the new tower to September 1878
2,000-gallon brick cistern added
Brick second floor added to the keeper's house (LighthouseFriends says 1882)
Front porch added to the keeper's house
Two red sectors placed in the light on 10 April 1894
Coal house remodeled to serve as an oil house
New model fourth-order lamps supplied; fog-bell hammer fall increased (Board report for the fiscal year ended 30 June 1899)
Porch erected; brick pavement and concrete floor laid (Board report for the fiscal year ended 30 June 1900)
Federal government acquired the island from the estate of C.C. Homer for Aberdeen Proving Ground; Coast Guard kept 6.94 acres
National Register form says automated in 1917 (LighthouseFriends says a keeper stayed until 1918)
Light changed from oil to acetylene and fog signal discontinued (LighthouseFriends); index lists a change in illuminant
Unwatched acetylene light and fog bell placed on a caisson near the south end of the island, November 1927
Decommissioned by the Coast Guard; lens removed; keeper's house later torn down
Army restoration of the tower; repainted, windows replaced (LighthouseFriends)
Listed on the National Register of Historic Places (NRIS 97000060)
More complete Army restoration, with masonry, lantern and windows (directory)
Solar-powered light installed; relit in September 2011

corrections.why: The National Register form gives the tower's total height as 40 ft 6 in (12.3 m). The stored 11.5 m matches the directory's focal plane (38 ft, 11.5 m), not the tower height.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Board's 1899 report records new fourth-order lamps, not a lens. The NRHP's 1899 'fourth-order Fresnel lamp' most likely describes that work, so the 1855 lens date from LighthouseFriends and the archive is not contradicted. The story gives 1855 for the lens and records the 1899 work as lamps.

notes_for_editor: Method: the full NRHP registration form (read in full), the US Lighthouse Society archive place and roster, LighthouseFriends (facts only; paraphrased), Light-House Board reports for 1891-92, 1894, 1896-97, 1899 and 1900 (scan pages), the Lighthouse Service Bulletin index for 1918-1923 (entry only: the OCR of the 1918 narrative did not turn up under the station's name), the 1928 Bulletin, and Rowlett's Maryland directory. Conflicts left open: nine oil lamps (NRHP) against thirteen lamps and reflectors (LighthouseFriends); fog-bell tower rebuilt 1878 (LighthouseFriends) or 1879 (NRHP); second floor on the keeper's house 1882 (LighthouseFriends) or 1883 (NRHP); tower height 40 ft 6 in total (NRHP, LighthouseFriends) against 30 ft from base to lantern (archive); automation in 1917 (NRHP) against removal of the last keeper in 1918 (LighthouseFriends; the archive roster ends with Simpson in 1918); LighthouseFriends calls Cohee the last keeper, which the roster contradicts. The Bulletin's 1927 station text is OCR-garbled ('Pool,es I sland Bar', date 'November W, 19,27'); the November 1927 date rests on LighthouseFriends and the OCR. The 1927 caisson light has its own station record (us-md-pooles-island-2, 'Pooles Island Light / Pooles Island Bar Light'); this story only mentions it. No storm, wreck or rescue event tied to this station was found in the sources read, so that chapter is omitted. The Baltimore Sun 2011 article is cited only through LighthouseFriends; it was not read. Descendants and volunteers named in that account are not named here. The Aberdeen Proving Ground commander is named only by public role. Checked against the page images and the cached texts: the 1928 Bulletin (PDF p. 3, image) reads 'November 29, 1927' and places the unwatched station marking Pooles Island Bar; the story treats that caisson light as a separate light, not the 1825 tower. The distance on that page is not quoted, because the OCR and the image differ on the numeral. The Light-House Board volumes are cited by their fiscal years (ended 30 June 1892, 1899 and 1900); the 1894 and 1896-97 items read as stated (scan pp. 423, 351). The 1918-1923 index entry (PDF p. 30) reads 'Pooles Island, change in illuminant' as stated. Disagreements now stated in the story: second floor 1882 (LighthouseFriends) or 1883 (NRHP); tower height 40 ft 6 in (NRHP), 44 ft (directory), and 30 ft from base to lantern (archive).
